96 {OCR?} and they set out.
And Heraclius sent to the Khagan, the king of the Khazars, to send him forty thousand troops to march against the Persians,
and he promised to give him his daughter Eudocia in marriage.
Now Khosrow, when he heard that Shahrbaraz had rebelled,
and that Heraclius was now descending into his country,
his soul grew faint,
and he was distressed.
And he gathered an army as best he could,
and appointed Ruzbihan as their leader.
And when the Persians encountered the Romans, the Persians were defeated,
and Ruzbihan was killed.
And when Khosrow heard,
he fled from Dastagird {OCR: Sqwtʾ / Sāqartā} where he was staying.
And Heraclius pursued after him,
and plundered his treasuries and his wealth.
Now Sheroe {Shirin}, the son of Khosrow,
who had been imprisoned by his father,
came out of prison,
and pursued after Khosrow his father and killed him,
and reigned after him for nine months.
And Heraclius, when he returned to winter in Edessa,
Sheroe sent to inform him of the murder of his father,
and made peace with him,
on condition that the Persians should depart from the territories of the Romans.
Now Sheroe, having reigned for nine months, died.
And Ardashir reigned after him for one year and nine (ten) months.
And this one was killed by Shahrbaraz, the one who was with Heraclius,
and he himself reigned,
and confirmed the covenant and the treaty with him.
And in the year six of the Arabs, half of the half of the sun's disk was dimmed,
and there was darkness from the first Tishrin until Haziran,
so that people said
that the disk of the sun would never again be restored {OCR?}.
And there was a plague, that is, a disease of tumours, in Palestine,
and myriads of people died from it.
Section.
The chroniclers say
that King Heraclius,
when the forces of the Arab Nomads reached him and seized territories,
assembled all the bishops, the chief priests, and the rest of the satraps,
and questioned them about the matter,
"How and what are these things?" And when each one of them answered according to what his understanding attained,
until the matter was left to him,
he then answered thus:
"I see that this people, in their conduct, their ways, and their faith,
are like the deep dawn in dim light, in which there is neither complete darkness,
nor is it endowed with full and splendid light."
And they demanded from him an explanation of the word,
and he answered:
"Yes, they are far"
